operations.old: Hastie et al.’s rigorous double-descent model has iid pairs y=xᵀβ+ε, independent centered noise variance σ², iid isotropic feature entries of mean zero/unit variance/finite 4+η moment, ||β||²=r² and p/n→γ. The almost-sure design-conditional risk is σ²γ/(1−γ) for γ<1 and r²(1−1/γ)+σ²/(γ−1) for γ>1. It diverges at γ=1, can decline on the overparameterized side as variance falls, and tends to null risk r² as γ→∞; it is not monotonically decreasing immediately for all SNR, and in the well-specified isotropic case the global minimum remains underparameterized.
operations.new: The local rigorous double-descent theorem uses one infinite real iid feature array with mean zero, unit variance and finite fourth moment, its upper-left n-by-p_n blocks, deterministic signal norm r≥0, and independent centered noise of variance σ² and independent isotropic test features. Carry the Axiom of Choice from the actual random-matrix suppliers. For p_n/n→γ∈(0,∞) with γ≠1, the almost-sure design-conditional risk is σ²γ/(1−γ) below one and r²(1−1/γ)+σ²/(γ−1) above one. The zero-signal branch is proved by cancellation of the risks for signals e1 and 2e1; the component lemma separately gives kernel-projection bias and signal-independent variance. The one-sided formulas diverge at γ=1 only for positive noise; they assert no limit at γ=1. With σ>0 the global infimum0 is approached as γ decreases to0 and is not attained, while noise-free zero risk is attained on the underparameterized branch. With σ>0 the overparameterized curve strictly decreases for r≤σ; when r>σ>0 its unique minimum is γ=r/(r−σ); at σ=0 it increases for r>0. These finite-fourth-moment claims use the actual local RMT proof, not an attribution of that broader moment class to the stronger-moment source proofs.

operations.new: For the RKHS result, fully prove lem-dense-cube-polynomial-norming-and-reproduction: elementary interior Bernstein from finite Fejér sums, central-cube extrapolation, polynomial damping and a compact convex-hull coefficient argument give reproduction weights with variation exp(Cn) whenever n h is sufficiently small. This applies to arbitrary finite h-dense sets without grid or separation assumptions. Use the Gaussian feature expansion and its factorial tail to prove the full power-function rate C exp(−c |log h|/h), then the existing orthogonal-projection and iid fill-distance proofs yield the stated noiseless interpolation bound. No Wendland/Madych–Nelson theorem remains an unproved premise, and no Gaussian Fourier/native-space extension theorem is assumed.
